scope_note: Complete retained built-in public catalogue plus separately attributed historical collections. All indexed normalized source records are available; geography, periods, units, missingness and source definitions remain attached. Overlapping source records are not independent people, places or shipments.

series.label: Median household income · 2024 dollars
series.unit: 2024 U.S. dollars per household per year
series.description: Published ACS B19013_E001 median household money income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars; B19013_M001 is its published 90% MOE. This is a household median, not mean per capita personal income or a regional-price-adjusted measure.

series.label: Real personal income per person
series.description: Published SARPI line 2. Real personal income is adjusted by BEA regional price parities and the national PCE price index, expressed in constant 2017 dollars, then divided by midyear population. This is a per-person average, not a household median, wage, disposable-income estimate or observation for each individual.

series.label: Real consumer spending per person
series.description: Published SARPI line 4. Total real personal consumption expenditures divided by total midyear population, in constant 2017 dollars. PCE includes consumption purchased on households’ behalf; it is not a cash household budget or the spending of a typical individual.

series.label: Median monthly gross rent
series.description: Published ACS B25064_E001 median gross rent. Gross rent is contract rent plus estimated average monthly tenant-paid utilities/fuels; B25064_M001 is the published 90% MOE.

series.label: Median gross rent as % of household income
series.description: Published ACS B25071_E001 median gross rent as a percentage of household income; B25071_M001 is the published 90% margin in percentage points. This direct published household-ratio median is not annualized median rent divided by median household income.

series.label: Regional price parity · All items
series.description: The term "all items" refers to all the detailed consumption goods and services used in the estimation of the RPPs. Published SARPP line 1; common BEA RPP scale. The 2024 published U.S. all items index is 100, retained as the comparison reference. No component has been rescaled to 100.

series.label: Regional price parity · Goods
series.description: Goods refer to durable and nondurable consumption goods used in the estimation of the RPPs. Goods categories include apparel, education, food, housing, medical, recreation, transportation, and other goods. Published SARPP line 2; common BEA RPP scale. The 2024 published U.S. goods index is 99.567, retained as the comparison reference. No component has been rescaled to 100.

series.label: Regional price parity · Housing services / rents
series.description: Housing expenditures consist of the monetary rents paid by tenants for tenant-occupied housing, an imputed rental value for owner-occupied dwellings (measured as the income the homeowner could have received if the house had been rented to a tenant), the rental value of farm dwellings, and spending on group housing. Housing price levels are only estimated for tenant-occupied housing. Published SARPP line 3; common BEA RPP scale. The 2024 published U.S. housing services / rents index is 100.629, retained as the comparison reference. No component has been rescaled to 100. Housing price levels are estimated from tenant-occupied rents; this is not a home-purchase-price index.

series.label: Regional price parity · Utilities
series.description: Household utilities consist of water supply and sanitation and electricity and gas. Published SARPP line 4; common BEA RPP scale. The 2024 published U.S. utilities index is 98.441, retained as the comparison reference. No component has been rescaled to 100.

series.label: Regional price parity · Other services
series.description: Other services refer to services consumption products, except rents, that are used in the estimation of the RPPs. Other services categories include education, food, housing, medical, recreation, transportation, and other services. Published SARPP line 5; common BEA RPP scale. The 2024 published U.S. other services index is 100.147, retained as the comparison reference. No component has been rescaled to 100.

series.label: Fertilizer consumption (kilograms per hectare of arable land) · annual history
series.unit: kilograms per hectare of arable land
series.commodity: Fertilizer consumption (kilograms per hectare of arable land)
series.definition: Fertilizer consumption measures the quantity of plant nutrients used per unit of arable land. Fertilizer products cover nitrogenous, potash, and phosphate fertilizers (including ground rock phosphate). Traditional nutrients--animal and plant manures--are not included. For the purpose of data dissemination, FAO has adopted the concept of a calendar year (January to December). Some countries compile fertilizer data on a calendar year basis, while others are on a split-year basis. Arable land includes land defined by the FAO as land under temporary crops (double-cropped areas are counted once), temporary meadows for mowing or for pasture, land under market or kitchen gardens, and land temporarily fallow. Land abandoned as a result of shifting cultivation is excluded. Original provider: FAO electronic files and web site, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

series.label: Fertilizer consumption (% of fertilizer production) · annual history
series.definition: Fertilizer consumption measures the quantity of plant nutrients and is calculated as production plus imports minus exports. Fertilizer products cover nitrogenous, potash, and phosphate fertilizers (including ground rock phosphate). Traditional nutrients--animal and plant manures--are not included. Because some chemical compounds used for fertilizers have other industrial applications, the consumption data may overstate the quantity available for crops. Fertilizer consumption as a share of production shows the agriculture sector's vulnerability to import and energy price fluctuation. Most fertilizers that are commonly used in agriculture contain the three basic plant nutrients-nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Some fertilizers also contain certain micronutrients such as zinc and other metals that are necessary for plant growth. Materials that are applied to the land primarily to enhance soil characteristics (rather than as plant food) are commonly referred to as soil amendments. Original provider: FAO electronic files and web site, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

Sources: Coal, Natural Gas, and Petroleum: Energy in the American Economy, 1850-1975, Table VII. Conventional Hydroelectric Power: Energy in the American Economy, 1850-1975, Table II.
